run.question: 配置的业务数据库里有哪些表？orders 表里每种 status 的订单各有多少条、failed 占比多少？请用数据库只读查询工具核实后回答。

report.summary: The configured SQL Server database (target m0-otel-20260909, source otel-demo) contains exactly one table, dbo.orders, with columns id (int, PK), customer (varchar), status (varchar), amount (decimal). A GROUP BY query on status returned three groups: paid 144, failed 72, refunded 24; a separate whole-table aggregate confirmed total_rows 240, failed_rows 72, null_status_rows 0, so failed is 30.00% of all orders. All readings are the database as it is at query time (2026-11-20T21:29:4xZ), not a historical incident-window state. No incident, fault or health conclusion is drawn here: this was a data-inventory question only, so no Kubernetes, trace or metric evidence was consulted and no root cause is named.

claims.text: The configured database (dialect mssql, source otel-demo) lists exactly one user table: dbo.orders (table, schema dbo).

dbo.orders has four columns: id (int, not nullable, ordinal 1), customer (varchar, nullable, ordinal 2), status (varchar, nullable, ordinal 3), amount (decimal, nullable, ordinal 4); its only index is the unique primary-key index PK__orders__3213E83FAAE90874 on id, with no foreign keys.
Grouping dbo.orders by status returned exactly three rows: status 'paid' = 144, status 'failed' = 72, status 'refunded' = 24.

A whole-table aggregate on dbo.orders returned total_rows = 240, failed_rows = 72, null_status_rows = 0 and failed_pct = 30, so the 'failed' share of orders is 30.00% (72 of 240) and no order has a NULL status.

gaps: All results are the database state at query time (observed 2026-11-20T21:29:45Z to 2026-11-20T21:29:48Z), not the state during the authorized window ending 2026-11-20T21:29:43Z; historical row values are unknown.

Only tables visible to the read-only account are listed; a table invisible to that account, or beyond the listing limit, would not appear, so 'only one table' is a statement about what this query returned.
The database exposes no timestamps on orders, so whether the failed orders accumulated in any particular period cannot be determined from these queries.
next_steps: If the failed-order rate needs an operational interpretation, correlate dbo.orders rows with payment service error signals and logs over a matching window, since this run only verified the database counts.

query.sql: SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM dbo.orders GROUP BY status ORDER BY cnt DESC

SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_rows, SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'failed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS failed_rows, SUM(CASE WHEN status IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS null_status_rows, CAST(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'failed' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*) AS decimal(10,2)) AS failed_pct FROM dbo.orders
